newsitem.title: UKRAINE: UKRAINE FINAL BUDGET DRAFT READY FRIDAY-MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: UKRAINE FINAL BUDGET DRAFT READY FRIDAY-MINISTER.

text.p: Ukraine will submit to parliament tomorrow the final version of the much-delayed budget, set to pave the way for billions of dollars in foreign credits, the Economy Minister said on Thursday.
Yuri Yekhanurov also told reporters the document, which was due on January 1, would be passed by the end of next month.

"The government will officially hand over the draft budget to parliament on Friday, and we expect it to get second reading from May 12 to 16, and then to be passed by the end of May," Yekhanurov said.
He said the final draft forecast a deficit of 5.73 billion hryvnia's from a projected gross domestic product (GDP) of 100.4 billion hryvnias.
A deficit equivalent to 5.8 percent of GDP, or four percent by Western calculations, was agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) late last year.
Once the budget is passed, along with a package of tax reforms to underpin it, the IMF is expected to lend Ukraine a $2.5 to $3 billion, three-year Extended Fund Facility (EFF).

A total of 2.40 billion hryvnias of the deficit would be covered with foreign credits, 1.63 billion hryvnias would come from the Treasury-bill market, and the central bank would cover the final 1.70 billion hryvnias, the government has said.
Yekhanurov said the central bank would not be required to issue direct credits to the government, a practice which in the past led to skyrocketing inflation.
He did not mention Ukraine's intention to issue foreign bonds, which it has promised to do this year.
The budget, based on the new tax reform laws expected to come into effect on July 1, foresees revenues at 19.95 billion hryvnias and expenditures at 25.68 billion hryvnias.
Central bank chief Viktor Yushchenko said earlier this month Ukraine would raise between $300 and $900 million from Eurobonds or samurai bonds to finance the deficit.
The government has forecast inflation at about 25 percent this year from 39.7 percent in 1996.

Parliament handed back the budget, requesting changes to it, late last year after being presented with a revised draft budget last November. Ukraine has not passed a budget on time since independence in 1991.
